title: Chapter 114 — Crossing Over: From Top Seller to Sales Leader
intro: The job that changes, the first ninety days, and the ex-peer problem.

sections.title: The Job Changes
sections.content:
Sales leadership is a different profession. Your output shifts from your number to their numbers. The skills that made you a top seller — closing ability, product knowledge, customer relationships — are necessary but no longer sufficient.

As a leader, your job is to make 8-12 other people better. Every hour you spend coaching returns more revenue than any hour you spend closing personally. If you cannot let go of being the top seller, you cannot be the top leader.

sections.title: The Ex-Peer Problem
sections.content:
Yesterday you were peers. Today you are their manager. This is the hardest transition in sales leadership.

Be direct about it. 'I know this is a change. My job is to help you sell more and earn more. I am going to be honest with you — that is what you would want from a good manager, and that is what I am going to give you.'

Do not try to be their friend and their boss. Be fair, be consistent, be honest. The respect will follow from the results you help them achieve.

sections.title: The First 90 Days as Leader
sections.content:
Month 1: observe. Watch every rep with customers. Take notes. Understand the current strengths and gaps on the floor before you change anything.

Month 2: coach. Start one-on-ones. Give specific, actionable feedback. Focus on one improvement per rep — not five. Build trust through competence and fairness.

Month 3: systematize. Implement the huddle if there is not one. Clean up the CRM. Establish the scorecard. Set clear expectations with specific numbers.

Do not change everything at once. The team needs to trust you before they will follow you.
